1. Heard Mr. R. De, learned counsel for the petitioner Kishore Kumar Das and Mr. R.G. Barua,
learned Addl. P.P. for the State of Assam.

2. By this application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 [Cr.PC], the petitioner has approached this Court seeking the benefit of pre-arrest bail, apprehending his arrest,
in connection with BI(EO) Police Station Case No. 04/2022 under Sections Page No.# 2/2 120(B)/420/406/409 IPC.

sentences.text: Several fraudulent transactions were unearthed during preliminary internal investigation which reveals creation of void mortgages, irregularities in the documentation, misappropriation of funds from the loan account, conspiracies to defraud the Bank etc., all perpetrated by Md. Fidusur Rahman, Proprietor of M/s Chandrapur Rural Ware House.
A Term Loan of Rs. 300.00 Lacs was sanctioned on 23.03.2012.
The personal guarantors for Md. Fidusur Rahman also created equitable mortgages of their individual landed properties.

Due to non-repayment of loan and during the currency of the loan and after the loan account was classified as NPA, on 31.03.2014 the Bank has initiated recovery proceeding under the provisions of the SARFAESI Act.
4. It is submitted by the learned Addl. P.P. that the Case Diary reveals that several inconsistencies regarding the sanction, transaction and creation of security were detected.
The conduct of the guarantors as well as bank employees also came under cloud.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has co- operated with the investigation.
His statement has already been recorded.
6. I have perused the Case Dairy.
There are indeed incriminating materials against the present petitioner.
I have considered the age of the petitioner.
He is a retired person.
He has co-operated with the investigation and has not violated bail conditions.
7. In view of my foregoing discussions, the interim order dated 15.07.2022 is hereby made absolute.
